key_insight: Self-Building Labs (SBL) turns laboratory automation from a fixed, pre-engineered system into one that can design and assemble the missing lab capabilities needed to pursue a high-level scientific goal.
engineering_relevance: This shifts the bottleneck in autonomous experimentation from manual reconfiguration and programming to scalable, goal-driven lab synthesis across different robots and setups.
method: Starts from existing infrastructure, from an empty room to a working self-driving lab.
Automatically builds the missing pieces: lab layout, digital twin, robot skills, and experimental workflows.
Supports multi-robot operation and adapts to different laboratory configurations.
evidence_signal: The paper reports end-to-end validation across multiple robot/setup configurations, including a real-world quantum-dot synthesis experiment.
watch_item: A practical concern is that self-building still depends on reliable integration of hardware, simulation, and control software, which may be difficult to generalize across diverse lab environments.
